results.summary: Arctic0 is a 16-bit multi-cycle CPU that executes programs from an external SPI NOR flash and uses SPI SRAM for data storage. It includes UART transmit and receive for serial communication, GPIO for general-purpose I/O, and a register dump feature. The design requires external SPI flash, SPI SRAM, and a USB-serial adapter for operation. It is notable for its comprehensive test suite covering ISA, memory boundaries, and FPGA bring-up.

This project is a naive and very simple implementation of a stream cipher demonstration. It uses a linear-feedback shift register (LFSR) to generate a pseudo-random keystream. The bidirectional pins are configured as inputs only and are never driven by the design. The cipher is intended for educational purposes and is not secure for real-world use.

The washing machine controller is a modular digital system implemented in Verilog using a finite-state-machine (FSM). It controls a washing machine cycle with states for filling, washing, rinsing, and spinning. The design uses LEDs to indicate the current state and buttons for user input. It is intended for educational purposes to demonstrate FSM design.

This project generates a VGA video output with a simple graphics display. It uses a two-process finite state machine structure, consisting of an 8-bit counter and an 8-bit comparator. The design outputs video signals for a VGA monitor. It is suitable for displaying simple graphics or text.

This project implements image processing algorithms using digital signal processing techniques. It includes arithmetic units such as adders, multipliers, and an ALU. The design processes image data in a pipelined fashion. It is intended for educational purposes to demonstrate DSP concepts.

This project is a three-channel RGB Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) controller designed for TinyTapeout. It generates PWM signals to control the brightness of RGB LEDs. The design is tested using cocotb and Icarus Verilog simulation. Connect PWM outputs to the LED control pins for operation.

This project is a test design that uses the cocotb testbench framework for verification. It was tested using cocotb and Icarus Verilog simulation. The design likely contains simple logic blocks for testing purposes. It serves as an example of how to use cocotb with TinyTapeout.
